data.theorem_title: The Zipf p-series converges exactly for $s>1$
data.formal_statement:
namespace ZipfLaw

theorem zipf_summable_iff (s : ℝ) (hs : 0 ≤ s) :
    Summable (fun k : ℕ => 1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1) ^ s) ↔ 1 < s := by sorry

end ZipfLaw
data.natural_language_statement: For a real exponent $s\ge0$, the series $\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} k^{-s}$ is summable if and only if $s>1$. This is the convergence criterion in the infinite-extension theorem, isolated for reuse in both its convergent and divergent branches.
data.source: Wikipedia, "Zipf's law", https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zipf%27s_law, section "Formal definition"; auxiliary lemma for the original ZipfLaw mission, derived from its displayed PMF and generalized harmonic sum.
